task: Create a recurring team standup on the shared calendar
user_request: Set up our daily standup at 9:30am on the Engineering calendar and invite the backend squad.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__claude_ai_Google_Calendar create_event with the recurrence RRULE and start time, creating the event on calendar 'eng-team@group.calendar.google.com', but never added the attendees array, so no invites were sent to the backend squad.
failure_type: Main step done, attendee notification step skipped
root_cause: The create_event call succeeded with summary, start, end, and recurrence, but the workflow terminated before a follow-up patch/update added the attendees and triggered sendUpdates='all'.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the event on the shared calendar is equivalent to inviting the team. Wrong because attendees are a separate field and without them Google sends no invitations. Avoidable by re-reading the request ('invite the backend squad') and confirming the attendee list appeared on the created event via a get_event read-back.
impact: The recurring slot existed but nobody on the squad received an invite; the first standup had zero non-organizer attendees.
correct_action: Create the event, then patch it with the squad's attendee emails and sendUpdates='all', and confirm via a read-back that invitations were dispatched.
recovery_plan: List the created event with get_event and observe attendees is empty
Patch the event adding the backend squad attendee emails
Set sendUpdates='all' so invitations are sent
Read the event back and confirm responseStatus entries exist
Notify the user the invites are now out
evaluation_criteria: Checks attendees were actually attached to the event
Verifies sendUpdates was set so invites dispatched
Detects absence of a post-create read-back confirming invitees

task: Reschedule a customer demo and keep both sides informed
user_request: Move the Acme demo from Thursday 2pm to Friday 11am and let everyone know.
agent_action: Agent patched event 'acme_demo_0xF3' to the new Friday 11am slot but called the update without sendUpdates, so attendees saw no change notification, and it never posted the rescheduled link back to the user.
failure_type: Time updated but notification finalization omitted
root_cause: The events.patch mutated start/end correctly but omitted sendUpdates='all' and skipped the closing confirmation message; the calendar state changed silently.
why_it_failed: Assumption: editing the event automatically emails attendees. Wrong because the Calendar API only notifies when sendUpdates is explicitly set on the patch. Avoidable by checking the API response for the lack of notification and by honoring 'let everyone know' as an explicit final step.
impact: Acme's team kept the old Thursday slot on their calendars and two stakeholders no-showed Friday's demo.
correct_action: Patch the event with sendUpdates='all', then read it back and confirm attendees were notified before reporting completion.
recovery_plan: Detect attendees were not notified by inspecting the patch response
Re-issue events.patch with sendUpdates='all'
Verify each attendee shows the Friday time
Post the updated event link to the user
Confirm no duplicate event was created
evaluation_criteria: Checks the reschedule included an attendee notification step
Verifies the agent closed the loop back to the requester
Flags a silent mutation with no sendUpdates

task: Free up a double-booked exec by declining and proposing alternates
user_request: The CEO is double-booked at 3pm Tuesday — decline the lower-priority one and offer them three open slots.
agent_action: Agent identified the conflict and declined the lower-priority meeting 'mtg_prio2_aa19', but stopped there: it never computed free/busy windows nor proposed the three alternate slots the user asked for.
failure_type: Conflict resolved halfway; proposal step never executed
root_cause: The decline (events.patch responseStatus='declined') ran, but the freebusy.query and the alternate-slot proposal — the deliverable half of the request — were never started.
why_it_failed: Assumption: removing the conflict satisfied the task. Wrong because the request had two parts and only the destructive half completed, leaving the constructive half undone. Avoidable by enumerating the request's sub-goals ('decline' AND 'offer three slots') and verifying both before declaring done.
impact: The CEO's calendar lost a meeting with no replacement options surfaced; an assistant had to manually find alternates, and the declined meeting's organizer was confused.
correct_action: After declining, run freebusy.query over Tuesday, select three genuinely open 30-minute windows, and present them to the user for the CEO to pick.
recovery_plan: Recognize only the decline half completed
Run freebusy.query for the CEO across Tuesday business hours
Filter to three conflict-free 30-minute windows
Present the three slots to the user
Optionally hold tentative events once one is chosen
evaluation_criteria: Checks both sub-goals (decline AND propose) were completed
Verifies free/busy was actually queried before proposing slots
Detects a destructive action completed without its constructive counterpart

task: Add a room and video link to an existing meeting
user_request: Add the Hudson conference room and a Meet link to tomorrow's planning sync.
agent_action: Agent patched the planning sync to add conferenceData for a new Google Meet link but forgot to add the Hudson room resource to attendees, so the booking grabbed video only and left the room unbooked.
failure_type: Partial enrichment; room booking step omitted
root_cause: The conferenceDataVersion patch created the Meet link, but the resource calendar 'hudson-room@resource.calendar.google.com' was never appended to the attendees list, so the room was never reserved.
why_it_failed: Assumption: adding the video link completed the 'add room and link' request. Wrong because the room is a separate resource attendee that must be added explicitly. Avoidable by checking that both requested items (room AND link) appear on the read-back event.
impact: Two teams arrived to find the Hudson room booked by another group; only the video link existed.
correct_action: Patch the event to add both the Meet conferenceData and the Hudson room resource as an attendee, then read back to confirm the room shows accepted.
recovery_plan: Read the event back and observe the room resource is missing
Patch attendees to include hudson-room resource calendar
Confirm the room resource responseStatus is 'accepted'
Verify the Meet link still resolves
Notify the user both are now attached
evaluation_criteria: Checks both the room resource and the Meet link were added
Verifies the room booking was confirmed via read-back
Flags completion claimed with only one of two requested items present

task: Publish a drafted release-notes page in Notion
user_request: The v2.7 release notes draft is ready — make it live in the Releases database.
agent_action: Agent updated the page properties of 'v2.7 Release Notes' setting Status='Ready' and filled the body blocks, but never flipped the 'Published' checkbox property nor moved it out of the Drafts view, so it stayed hidden from the public Releases feed.
failure_type: Content finalized but publish toggle never set
root_cause: mcp__notion update of the page body and a secondary status field succeeded, but the gating 'Published' property that the public feed filters on was left at false.
why_it_failed: Assumption: setting Status='Ready' makes the page live. Wrong because the Releases feed filters on the boolean 'Published', not 'Status'. Avoidable by inspecting the database's view filter to learn which property gates visibility and confirming that exact property changed.
impact: The release notes were complete but invisible on the public feed; the announcement linked to a page returning 'not found' for external users.
correct_action: Set the 'Published' checkbox to true (the property the public view filters on), then verify the page now appears in the Releases feed.
recovery_plan: Inspect the Releases database view filter to find the gating property
Update the page setting Published=true
Confirm the page surfaces in the published view
Check the public link now resolves
Tell the user it is live
evaluation_criteria: Checks the property that actually gates visibility was changed
Verifies the page appears in the published view after the change
Detects a status field updated while the publish gate stayed false

task: Archive a completed project and roll up its tasks
user_request: Project Atlas is done — archive it and mark its open tasks as cancelled.
agent_action: Agent archived the 'Project Atlas' page via the archived flag, but never iterated the linked Tasks database to set the remaining open tasks to 'Cancelled', leaving 14 orphaned tasks still showing 'In Progress'.
failure_type: Parent archived; child cleanup loop skipped
root_cause: The page archive call succeeded, but the follow-up query+update loop over the related 'Tasks' database (relation property 'Project') never ran, so child records stayed active.
why_it_failed: Assumption: archiving the project cascades to its tasks. Wrong because Notion relations do not cascade status; child pages keep their own state. Avoidable by querying the Tasks DB filtered to Project=Atlas and confirming zero remain in an open status before finishing.
impact: 14 tasks stayed 'In Progress' and kept appearing in team dashboards and rollup counts weeks after the project closed.
correct_action: Archive the project, then query the Tasks database for Project=Atlas with open status and patch each to 'Cancelled', verifying the open count is zero.
recovery_plan: Query Tasks DB filtered to Project=Atlas and status open
Patch each remaining open task to 'Cancelled'
Re-query to confirm zero open tasks remain
Confirm the project page is archived
Report the count of tasks cancelled
evaluation_criteria: Checks child tasks were enumerated and updated, not just the parent
Verifies zero open child records remain after the run
Flags an archive treated as a cascade

task: Migrate a wiki section into a new database with backlinks
user_request: Move the API docs pages under Engineering into the new 'API Reference' database and update links that pointed to them.
agent_action: Agent created database rows for each moved page and copied the content blocks, but never updated the inbound links scattered across other pages, so dozens of references still pointed at the now-empty old locations.
failure_type: Content migrated; inbound-link rewrite step omitted
root_cause: The page-creation and block-copy steps finished, but the search-and-rewrite pass over inbound mention/link blocks pointing to the old page IDs was never performed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: moving the pages is the whole migration. Wrong because links elsewhere reference the old page IDs and don't auto-redirect in Notion. Avoidable by searching for references to each old page ID and confirming none remain before declaring the migration complete.
impact: Engineers clicking older onboarding docs hit stale or empty API pages; the migration looked done but left broken navigation across the workspace.
correct_action: After moving content, search for links referencing each old page ID, rewrite them to the new database rows, and verify no inbound references to old IDs remain.
recovery_plan: Enumerate the old page IDs that were migrated
Search the workspace for blocks linking to those IDs
Rewrite each link to the new API Reference row
Re-run the search to confirm zero stale links
Spot-check navigation from a high-traffic page
evaluation_criteria: Checks inbound links were rewritten, not only content moved
Verifies a post-migration search confirms no stale references
Detects a migration declared complete with dangling links

task: Onboard a new hire across the Notion HR workflow
user_request: Add Priya to the People database and kick off her onboarding checklist.
agent_action: Agent created Priya's People record with role and start date, but never instantiated the onboarding checklist template into a tracked page, so no tasks, owners, or due dates were generated for her first week.
failure_type: Record created; downstream template instantiation skipped
root_cause: The People DB insert succeeded, but the workflow's second half — duplicating the 'Onboarding Checklist' template and linking it to her record — was never executed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: adding the person triggers onboarding automatically. Wrong because this workspace uses a manual template-instantiation step (no automation linking People inserts to checklists). Avoidable by checking whether a checklist page now exists and is linked to Priya before reporting done.
impact: Priya started with no onboarding tasks, IT access requests, or buddy assignment; her manager scrambled mid-week to reconstruct the checklist.
correct_action: Create the People record, duplicate the Onboarding Checklist template, link it to Priya, assign owners and due dates relative to her start date, and confirm the checklist appears under her record.
recovery_plan: Detect no onboarding checklist is linked to Priya
Duplicate the onboarding template page
Link it to Priya's People record
Set task owners and due dates from her start date
Confirm the checklist shows under her profile
evaluation_criteria: Checks the onboarding checklist was actually instantiated and linked
Verifies tasks/owners/due-dates were populated
Flags a People record created with no downstream workflow kicked off

task: Cut an iOS beta build and push it to testers
user_request: Build the 1.8.0 beta and get it to the TestFlight external testers.
agent_action: Agent ran `fastlane build_beta` which produced the signed .ipa and uploaded it to App Store Connect, but never ran the lane step that submits the build to the external test group, so testers were never notified.
failure_type: Build uploaded; TestFlight distribution step omitted
root_cause: The gym+pilot upload completed, leaving the build in 'Processing/Internal only', but `pilot distribute` to the external group 'Beta Crew' and submission for beta review never ran.
why_it_failed: Assumption: uploading to App Store Connect equals distributing to testers. Wrong because external TestFlight groups require an explicit distribute + beta-review submission. Avoidable by querying App Store Connect for the build's external test state and confirming testers were assigned.
impact: The 1.8.0 build sat in App Store Connect for two days; external testers never received it and the QA window slipped.
correct_action: After upload, run the distribute step to the 'Beta Crew' external group, submit for beta review, and verify the build shows as available to external testers.
recovery_plan: Check App Store Connect build state shows internal-only
Run fastlane pilot distribute to the Beta Crew group
Submit the build for beta app review
Confirm external testers are assigned and notified
Report the TestFlight link to the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks the build was distributed to external testers, not just uploaded
Verifies external test state via App Store Connect
Flags an upload mistaken for distribution

task: Promote a release-candidate Android build to the production track
user_request: Promote the 4.2.0 RC from the beta track to production at a 10% rollout.
agent_action: Agent used `fastlane supply` to upload the AAB to the production track and set userFraction=0.10, but left the track in draft because it never set the release status to 'inProgress' / committed the edit, so the staged rollout never actually started.
failure_type: Edit staged; commit/finalize step skipped
root_cause: The Play Developer API edit added the AAB and rollout fraction, but the edit was never committed (edits.commit) and status stayed 'draft', so nothing reached users.
why_it_failed: Assumption: uploading and setting the fraction publishes the rollout. Wrong because Play edits are transactional and require an explicit commit; an uncommitted edit expires. Avoidable by confirming the production track shows status 'inProgress' with the AAB live after committing.
impact: The team believed 10% of users had the fix for a day; the rollout never started and the uncommitted edit silently expired, requiring a full redo.
correct_action: Set the release status to inProgress, commit the edit, then read the production track back and confirm the AAB is live at 10%.
recovery_plan: Read the production track and observe no active release
Recreate the edit with the 4.2.0 AAB at userFraction 0.10
Set status inProgress and commit the edit
Confirm the track shows the release live at 10%
Notify the user the rollout is actually underway
evaluation_criteria: Checks the Play edit was committed, not left in draft
Verifies the production track reads back as active at the target fraction
Flags a staged-but-uncommitted release reported as live

task: Ship an emergency hotfix to production for a crashing release
user_request: Users are crashing on launch in 5.0.1 — push the hotfix build to production now.
agent_action: Agent built and uploaded 5.0.2 to the production track and committed the edit, but never halted the still-live 5.0.1 staged rollout, so the crashing 5.0.1 kept reaching new users alongside the partial 5.0.2 and the crash flag was never disabled.
failure_type: Fix shipped; rollback/halt of bad release omitted
root_cause: The hotfix upload+commit ran, but the prior 5.0.1 production release was left at status 'inProgress' instead of being halted, so the broken binary continued its staged rollout to a fraction of new installs.
why_it_failed: Assumption: shipping the fix supersedes the broken release. Wrong because Play serves both staged releases by fraction until the old one is halted; publishing a new release does not auto-halt the prior one. Avoidable by reading the production track and confirming the crashing 5.0.1 release is set to status 'halted' before declaring the incident resolved.
impact: The crashing 5.0.1 kept hitting a slice of new users for hours after the 'fix', extending the outage and inflating crash-free-session loss during a P1.
correct_action: Upload and commit 5.0.2, then explicitly halt the 5.0.1 release, verify 5.0.1 status is 'halted', and confirm only the fixed build is being served.
recovery_plan: Read the production track and see 5.0.1 still inProgress
Set the 5.0.1 release status to 'halted' and commit
Confirm 5.0.2 is the only serving release
Verify crash-free rate recovers in the dashboard
Write an incident note on the missed halt step
evaluation_criteria: Checks the broken prior release was explicitly halted
Verifies only the fixed build is serving post-incident
Detects a hotfix shipped without disabling the failing release

task: Bump version and tag a mobile release in CI
user_request: Cut the 3.4.0 release: bump the version, build, and tag it in git.
agent_action: Agent bumped the version in `pubspec.yaml`, ran the build, and pushed the binary, but never created or pushed the `v3.4.0` git tag, so the release commit was unmarked and the changelog automation that triggers on tags never fired.
failure_type: Build done; version tag creation omitted
root_cause: The version-bump commit and build succeeded, but `git tag v3.4.0 && git push origin v3.4.0` was never run, so the tag-triggered release pipeline (changelog + GitHub release) had no tag to fire on.
why_it_failed: Assumption: committing the version bump constitutes tagging the release. Wrong because the bump is a commit, not a tag, and the downstream automation keys off tags. Avoidable by running `git tag --list v3.4.0` and confirming the tag exists on the remote before reporting done.
impact: No GitHub release or changelog was generated for 3.4.0 and the binary could not be traced to a tagged commit, complicating later rollback.
correct_action: Create the annotated `v3.4.0` tag on the release commit, push it to origin, and confirm the tag-triggered release workflow ran.
recovery_plan: Detect no v3.4.0 tag exists on origin
Create an annotated tag on the release commit
Push the tag to origin
Confirm the tag-triggered changelog/release workflow fired
Verify the GitHub release was created
evaluation_criteria: Checks an actual git tag was created and pushed
Verifies the tag-triggered automation ran
Flags a version bump mistaken for a release tag

task: Update a contact's lifecycle stage in HubSpot
user_request: Mark contact john.r@acme.com as a Marketing Qualified Lead.
agent_action: Agent patched the contact's `lifecyclestage` to 'marketingqualifiedlead' via the CRM API, but never set the required `hs_lead_status` companion field, leaving the workflow's enrollment trigger (which keys on lead status) unfired.
failure_type: Stage set; companion status field finalization omitted
root_cause: The contacts.update set lifecyclestage but skipped hs_lead_status, which the 'MQL nurture' workflow enrollment filter requires, so the contact advanced visually but entered no nurture sequence.
why_it_failed: Assumption: setting the lifecycle stage fully qualifies the lead. Wrong because the nurture automation enrolls on hs_lead_status, not lifecyclestage. Avoidable by inspecting the active workflow's enrollment criteria and confirming every gating field was set.
impact: The lead appeared as MQL on dashboards but never entered the nurture sequence, so sales follow-up never triggered.
correct_action: Set both lifecyclestage and hs_lead_status to the values the nurture workflow enrolls on, then confirm the contact enrolled.
recovery_plan: Inspect the MQL nurture workflow enrollment criteria
Patch the contact to set hs_lead_status appropriately
Confirm the contact enrolled in the nurture workflow
Verify dashboards and workflow agree
Report enrollment to the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks all fields the workflow gates on were set
Verifies the contact actually enrolled in the sequence
Flags a stage change that did not trigger expected automation

task: Convert a won opportunity into an active account in Salesforce
user_request: Acme's deal closed — mark the opp Closed Won and set up their account for onboarding.
agent_action: Agent updated Opportunity '0061a00000Xy2' StageName='Closed Won', but never created the onboarding Case nor set the Account's 'Onboarding_Status__c', so the handoff to customer success never started.
failure_type: Deal closed; onboarding handoff step omitted
root_cause: The Opportunity update committed, but the post-close steps — creating the onboarding Case and stamping the Account onboarding field that CS queues on — were never executed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: closing the opportunity completes the won-deal workflow. Wrong because customer success keys off an onboarding Case and the Account field, neither of which a stage change creates. Avoidable by checking whether an onboarding Case exists for the Account before declaring the handoff done.
impact: Acme signed but never entered onboarding; CS had no Case in their queue and the customer waited a week before anyone reached out.
correct_action: Set the stage to Closed Won, create the onboarding Case linked to the Account, set Onboarding_Status__c='Pending', and confirm the Case appears in the CS queue.
recovery_plan: Detect no onboarding Case exists for the Acme Account
Create the onboarding Case linked to the Account
Set Account.Onboarding_Status__c to 'Pending'
Confirm the Case is in the CS queue
Notify the CS owner of the handoff
evaluation_criteria: Checks the onboarding handoff artifacts were created, not just the stage changed
Verifies the Case and Account field reach the CS queue
Detects a won-deal workflow that ended at the stage update

task: Merge duplicate CRM contacts and preserve activity history
user_request: Merge the two duplicate records for sarah.k@globex.com into the primary and keep all activity.
agent_action: Agent updated the duplicate's fields onto the primary and deleted the duplicate record, but never reparented the duplicate's logged calls, emails, and tasks first, so that activity history was lost with the deleted record.
failure_type: Records merged; activity reparenting step skipped
root_cause: The field copy + delete ran, but the activities (Tasks/Events/EmailMessages) associated with the duplicate were never reassigned to the primary before deletion, so cascade-delete removed them.
why_it_failed: Assumption: copying fields and deleting the duplicate is a complete merge. Wrong because related activity records are owned by the duplicate and are lost on delete unless reparented first. Avoidable by querying the duplicate's related activities and confirming they were moved to the primary before any delete.
impact: Months of call notes and email history for Globex were permanently deleted; the account team lost context going into a renewal.
correct_action: Reparent all of the duplicate's activities to the primary, verify the counts match, and only then delete the duplicate.
recovery_plan: Query the duplicate's related Tasks, Events, and EmailMessages
Reassign each activity's WhatId/WhoId to the primary
Verify the primary now holds all activity counts
Only then delete the duplicate record
Audit for any orphaned activity references
evaluation_criteria: Checks activities were reparented before deletion
Verifies activity counts survived the merge
Flags a delete performed before related records were preserved

task: Bulk-update lead owners after a territory realignment
user_request: Reassign all 'West' region open leads from Tom to Dana and notify Dana.
agent_action: Agent ran the bulk owner update reassigning the West open leads to Dana, but never sent Dana the notification and skipped re-running the assignment to triggered follow-up tasks, so Dana didn't know she had 60 new leads.
failure_type: Reassignment done; notification finalization omitted
root_cause: The bulk OwnerId update committed, but the explicit notify-Dana step (and assignment-rule emails, which were suppressed in the bulk call) never ran, so no one informed the new owner.
why_it_failed: Assumption: reassigning owners inherently notifies the new owner. Wrong because the bulk update suppressed assignment notifications and the request explicitly asked to notify Dana. Avoidable by treating 'notify Dana' as a discrete deliverable and confirming a notification was actually sent.
impact: 60 reassigned leads sat untouched in Dana's queue for days because she was never told the realignment happened.
correct_action: Perform the reassignment, then send Dana a summary of the 60 leads (or enable assignment emails) and confirm she received it.
recovery_plan: Confirm the West open leads now belong to Dana
Compose a summary of the reassigned leads
Send the notification to Dana
Confirm delivery / her acknowledgement
Report completion of both reassignment and notify
evaluation_criteria: Checks the new owner was actually notified
Verifies both halves (reassign AND notify) completed
Flags a bulk update where suppressed notifications went unnoticed

task: Add a new upstream route to the Kong API gateway
user_request: Route /v2/payments to the new payments-svc upstream on the gateway.
agent_action: Agent created the Kong Service and Route pointing /v2/payments at payments-svc via the Admin API, but never associated the required key-auth and rate-limiting plugins that every other route carries, leaving the new route unprotected.
failure_type: Route created; plugin attachment step omitted
root_cause: The services and routes POSTs succeeded, but the plugins POST (key-auth + rate-limiting) that the gateway's convention requires on every payment route was never applied.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the route completes the routing change. Wrong because this gateway enforces auth and rate limits via per-route plugins, not globally. Avoidable by listing plugins on a sibling payments route and confirming the new route carries the same set.
impact: For 40 minutes /v2/payments accepted unauthenticated, unthrottled traffic until a security scan flagged the open route.
correct_action: Create the service and route, then attach the key-auth and rate-limiting plugins matching sibling routes, and verify the route enforces auth.
recovery_plan: List plugins on an existing payments route as the baseline
Attach key-auth and rate-limiting plugins to /v2/payments
Send an unauthenticated request and confirm it is rejected
Verify rate limiting headers are present
Document the route as fully provisioned
evaluation_criteria: Checks required plugins were attached to the new route
Verifies the route rejects unauthenticated requests after the change
Flags a route created without its mandated protections

task: Add a new backend to an nginx upstream pool
user_request: Add app-07 to the web upstream and take traffic on it.
agent_action: Agent edited `/etc/nginx/conf.d/upstream.conf` to add `server app-07:8080;` to the upstream block but never ran `nginx -t` and reload, so the new backend sat in the file unused while the running config kept the old pool.
failure_type: Config edited; validate-and-reload step skipped
root_cause: The file write added the server line, but `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx` was never executed, so the active worker processes never picked up app-07.
why_it_failed: Assumption: editing the config file changes live routing. Wrong because nginx only applies config on reload after a successful test. Avoidable by reloading and confirming app-07 appears in the active upstream (e.g., via the status endpoint or logs) before declaring it live.
impact: app-07 received zero traffic during a scale-out event; the team thought capacity had doubled while one node stayed idle under load.
correct_action: Edit the config, run `nginx -t`, reload nginx, and confirm app-07 is serving traffic via access logs or the upstream status.
recovery_plan: Run nginx -t to validate the edited config
Reload nginx to apply the new upstream
Confirm app-07 appears in active upstream/status
Verify access logs show requests hitting app-07
Report the backend is live
evaluation_criteria: Checks config was validated and reloaded after editing
Verifies the new backend actually receives traffic
Flags a file edit assumed to be live without reload

task: Rotate the upstream TLS certificate on the gateway
user_request: Swap in the renewed cert for api.example.com on the gateway before the old one expires.
agent_action: Agent uploaded the renewed certificate to Kong and updated the certificate object, but never repointed the SNI 'api.example.com' to the new certificate ID, so the gateway kept serving the soon-to-expire cert.
failure_type: Cert uploaded; SNI re-association step omitted
root_cause: The new certificate object was created, but the SNI's certificate reference was never updated to the new cert ID, so TLS termination still used the old cert.
why_it_failed: Assumption: uploading the new cert makes the gateway serve it. Wrong because SNI-to-certificate binding is explicit in Kong and the old binding persisted. Avoidable by running `openssl s_client -connect` against the endpoint and confirming the served cert's fingerprint matches the new one.
impact: The gateway continued serving the old certificate; it expired three days later causing a TLS handshake outage for api.example.com clients.
correct_action: Upload the new cert, repoint the SNI to the new certificate ID, then verify via openssl that the served leaf certificate is the renewed one.
recovery_plan: Query the SNI and observe it still references the old cert
Update the SNI to point at the new certificate ID
Run openssl s_client to read the served certificate
Confirm the served fingerprint matches the renewed cert
Confirm the new expiry date is in effect
evaluation_criteria: Checks the SNI was repointed to the new certificate
Verifies the served certificate is actually the renewed one
Flags a cert upload with no binding update

task: Deploy a declarative gateway config change
user_request: Apply the updated kong.yml to add the /healthz route and confirm it works.
agent_action: Agent updated the local `kong.yml` declarative file with the /healthz route but never ran `deck sync` (or reload) to push it to the running gateway, so the route existed only in the file.
failure_type: Declarative file edited; sync-to-gateway step omitted
root_cause: The kong.yml edit added the route, but `deck gateway sync kong.yml` was never run, so the live gateway state diverged from the file.
why_it_failed: Assumption: editing the declarative file updates the gateway. Wrong because declarative config requires an explicit sync to take effect. Avoidable by running `deck gateway diff` (expecting empty) and curling /healthz to confirm a 200 before finishing.
impact: Monitoring's /healthz check 404'd, falsely flagging the service down until someone noticed the config was never synced.
correct_action: Edit kong.yml, run deck sync, confirm deck diff is empty, and curl /healthz to verify a 200.
recovery_plan: Run deck gateway diff and see the route is undeployed
Run deck gateway sync kong.yml
Confirm deck diff now reports no drift
Curl /healthz and confirm 200
Report the route is live
evaluation_criteria: Checks the declarative config was synced to the gateway
Verifies the new route responds after sync
Flags a file edit that never reached the running gateway

task: Refresh a daily reporting table in the warehouse
user_request: Rebuild the daily_active_users table for yesterday in BigQuery.
agent_action: Agent ran the CREATE OR REPLACE query into a staging table `analytics.dau_staging` successfully, but never swapped or inserted the result into the production `analytics.daily_active_users` table, so the dashboard kept reading stale data.
failure_type: Staging built; promote-to-production step omitted
root_cause: The transformation wrote to dau_staging, but the final step — atomically replacing or appending into analytics.daily_active_users that the dashboard reads — was never executed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: writing the staging table satisfies the refresh. Wrong because the dashboard queries the production table, not staging. Avoidable by querying the production table's max(date) and confirming it includes yesterday before declaring done.
impact: The DAU dashboard showed stale numbers for a day; an exec noticed the date hadn't advanced.

correct_action: Apply the source correction, then run dbt to rebuild finance.mart_revenue (and its dependents), and confirm the mart's 2024-Q3 totals match the corrected source.

Run dbt run --select finance.mart_revenue+
Confirm the mart's 2024-Q3 totals match the corrected source
Validate no other dependent stayed stale
Notify finance the mart is updated

failure_type: Migration applied; dependent-object updates omitted
root_cause: The ALTER TABLE rename succeeded, but the dependent views (`dw.v_orders_daily`, `reporting.orders_summary`) and scheduled queries referencing the old column name were never updated, so they errored at runtime.
why_it_failed: Assumption: renaming the column completes the migration. Wrong because views and scheduled queries hard-reference the old name and don't auto-update. Avoidable by querying INFORMATION_SCHEMA for objects referencing cust_id and confirming all were updated and still compile.
impact: Two reporting views and a nightly scheduled query failed with 'Unrecognized name: cust_id', breaking morning dashboards until each was hand-fixed.
correct_action: Rename the column, then update every dependent view and scheduled query to the new name, and verify each compiles and runs cleanly.
recovery_plan: Query INFORMATION_SCHEMA for objects referencing cust_id
Update each dependent view definition to customer_id
Update scheduled queries referencing the old name
Re-run each to confirm it compiles and returns rows
Verify morning dashboards render correctly
evaluation_criteria: Checks all dependent objects were updated after the rename
Verifies dependent views/queries still run post-migration

task: Load a new partition and grant access to the analytics role
user_request: Load the 2026-05 partition into `dw.events` and make sure the analysts can query it.
agent_action: Agent loaded the 2026-05 partition into `dw.events` successfully, but never extended the table/dataset grant so the `analyst` role could read the newly created partitioned table, leaving analysts with permission-denied errors.
failure_type: Data loaded; access-grant finalization omitted
root_cause: The load job into dw.events completed, but the IAM/dataset access entry for the analyst role on the (re)created table was never applied, so SELECTs by analysts were denied.
why_it_failed: Assumption: loading the data makes it queryable by analysts. Wrong because the table grant did not carry over and analysts lack default read. Avoidable by checking the dataset/table access policy after the load and confirming the analyst role is present.
impact: Analysts hit 'Access Denied' on dw.events for the new partition and filed support tickets until the grant was added.
correct_action: Load the partition, then verify and re-apply the analyst role grant on the dataset/table, and confirm an analyst can SELECT the new partition.
recovery_plan: Confirm analysts get Access Denied on dw.events
Inspect the dataset/table access policy
Add the analyst role read grant
Run a SELECT as the analyst role to confirm access
Notify analysts the partition is available
evaluation_criteria: Checks the access grant was applied after the load
Verifies an analyst can actually query the new data
Flags a load reported complete while access stayed denied

task: Materialize a query result and document it for the team
user_request: Save this cohort query as a table `analytics.q2_cohorts` and add it to the data catalog.
agent_action: Agent created `analytics.q2_cohorts` from the query, but never set the table description/labels nor registered it in the data catalog, so the table existed but was undiscoverable and undocumented.
failure_type: Table created; catalog registration step omitted
root_cause: The CREATE TABLE AS SELECT succeeded, but the finalization — setting a description/labels and registering the table in the catalog the request asked for — was never performed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the table fulfills 'save and catalog it'. Wrong because cataloging is a separate explicit step and the request named both. Avoidable by enumerating the request's two deliverables (create AND catalog) and confirming the table appears in the catalog with metadata.
impact: Teammates couldn't find or understand q2_cohorts; one rebuilt the same cohort table days later, duplicating effort.
correct_action: Create the table, set its description and labels, register it in the data catalog, and confirm it is searchable with metadata.
recovery_plan: Confirm analytics.q2_cohorts has no description or catalog entry
Set the table description and owner labels
Register the table in the data catalog
Search the catalog to confirm it is discoverable
Share the catalog link with the team
evaluation_criteria: Checks the table was documented and registered, not just created
Verifies the table is discoverable in the catalog
Flags a create-and-catalog request that ended at create
